newsitem.title: USA: Search ongoing for new Michigan deputy treasurer.
newsitem.headline: Search ongoing for new Michigan deputy treasurer.

text.p: Michigan Treasurer Doug Roberts said Tuesday that it will be a couple of months before the state selects a new chief deputy treasurer to replace Nick Khouri.
In a telephone interview, Roberts also said that Khouri's replacement would probably not have most of his duties concentrated in the state's municipal bond issuance.
Instead, the new chief deputy treasurer would have more "overall responsibility" in the state's treasury department, with more of the bond work done by others within the department, Roberts added.
He said an outside firm was conducting a nation-wide search to fill the position Khouri held since 1991.

Late last month, the treasurer's office announced Khouri was leaving later this month for Guam where he will work for three months as a consultant. Khouri has said he plans to return to Lansing, Mich., in April to join the staff of Public Sector Consultants, a public policy organization.

In the meantime, Roberts said Roy Pentilla, an official with the both the Michigan Higher Education Facilities Authority and Michigan State Hospital Finance Authority, will take over day-to-day state bond business.
Roberts said Khouri, who resigned, would be missed. He added that resignations were normal at this time given that the state is in the middle of the second term of Gov. John Engler.
Roberts was appointed state treasurer by Engler in 1991.
